title: Juniper and the Ledger
premise: Estate lawyer Beatrix Dunmore is hired to execute the will of Edmund Voss, a reclusive industrialist whose death certificate predates his signature on the document. The will names an heir who officially never existed, and twin letters found in Voss's safe—one confessing to a thirty-year-old arson that killed a child, one promising 'more' to whoever finds them—pull Beatrix into a conspiracy among the town's founding families. As the statute of limitations ticks down, Beatrix discovers their own late mother was the alibi-witness who lied for Voss's circle, forcing them to choose between protecting her memory and exposing the truth. In the end, Beatrix publishes both letters at the reading of the final codicil, dismantling the heirs' claims and accepting that identity built on silence is no identity at all.
about_author: Kestrel Okafor is a former probate clerk turned novelist who spent a decade watching families fracture over paper. They write mysteries about the lies people notarize.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Beatrix Dunmore, meticulous and emotionally walled-off, accepts the Voss estate from a courier who vanishes before signing. Examining the documents, they find the death date precedes the signature by eleven days. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into unease—the first crack in their belief that cases are just paperwork.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: In Voss's wall safe, Beatrix finds two sealed letters: one confessing to the 1994 Harrow Mill fire that killed a child, one unsigned, promising 'more' to whoever reads them first. The named heir, 'Iris Voss,' appears in no registry. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: fascination overriding caution; they pocket the confession instead of logging it—their first ethical compromise.

chapters.title: The Town That Remembers Nothing
chapters.summary: Beatrix travels to Ashcombe, where the mill fire is a civic non-event: plaques scrubbed, records sealed. A retired archivist, Mabel Chen, hints the child's body was never identified. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: isolation deepens as they realize an entire town conspired to forget, and they are asking questions alone.

chapters.title: Heirs and Alibis
chapters.summary: The contesting heirs—Voss's nephew Gerald and the Halbrook family—retain a shark lawyer and produce airtight alibis for the night of the fire, all corroborated by the same witness: Margaret Dunmore, Beatrix's mother. POV: Beatrix, with a flashback fragment. Emotional beat: vertigo; the case has reached into their own history.

chapters.title: What Mother Kept
chapters.summary: Sorting Margaret's effects, Beatrix finds a train ticket dated the night of the fire—she wasn't in Ashcombe to alibi anyone. Someone forged her testimony. POV: Beatrix, alternating with Mabel. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into resolve; loyalty to a dead mother now wars with the truth she may have died protecting.

chapters.title: Iris
chapters.summary: Mabel identifies Iris Voss: the child who supposedly died in the fire, smuggled out by her father Edmund and declared dead to escape the Halbrooks. The confession letter was Edmund's insurance; the second letter is Iris's own, still alive and writing. POV: Mabel. Emotional beat: tenderness and dread—the 'victim' is the most dangerous person in the story.

chapters.title: The Second Letter's Terms
chapters.summary: A meeting with Iris, disguised as the estate's cleaning contractor, reveals her terms: full acknowledgment or she releases evidence implicating the Halbrooks in the arson—and Margaret in the cover-up. She offers Beatrix a cut. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: temptation and fury; power corrupting even the wronged party, mirroring what destroyed the founders.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Gerald Halbrook, panicking as the legal deadline nears, breaks into Beatrix's office for the letters and finds only copies—he's being watched too. Beatrix realizes someone inside the estate has been feeding Iris information. POV: Gerald, then Beatrix. Emotional beat: rising panic on all sides; every player now acts out of self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: At the final codicil reading, Beatrix produces both letters publicly, revealing Iris alive, the forged alibi, and the Halbrooks' crime—but also naming Margaret's complicity, sacrificing their mother's reputation. Iris, seeing Beatrix refuse the bribe, withdraws her extortion demand. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: climax—truth delivered at maximum cost, loyalty and honesty finally forced onto the same scale.

chapters.title: Signature
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the estate settles; Iris takes her name legally, and Mabel restores the fire's true record. Beatrix, changed, takes on a pro bono case for another erased heir—no longer invisible themselves. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; identity rebuilt on truth rather than silence, the ledger finally balanced.
